setup: Hook your legs under the decline pads
Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades back
Grip a little wider than your shoulders
execution: Breathe in, brace, unrack to straight arms
Lower to your lower chest under control
Press up and slightly back over shoulders
Breathe at the top, then the next rep
faults: Don't bounce the bar off your chest
Don't let your elbows flare wide
Don't let your feet slip off the pads

notes: Use a spotter, or a decline station with safety catches. You can't roll a stuck bar off your chest in a decline as easily as on a flat bench.
Agree the lift-off and the help signal with your spotter before the set.
Wrap your thumbs round the bar. Avoid a thumbless grip.
Sit up slowly after the set; being head-down can leave you light-headed.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at bench height, head end low on the left, decline bench about 15–30° with the leg pads on the right. Uprights drawn behind the figure.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Lying head-down on a decline bench, knees hooked under the pads. Arms straight and vertical, bar over the shoulders. Upper back set, shoulder blades pulled together.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Bar touching the lower chest, below the nipple line. Forearms near vertical, elbows tucked a little toward the body. Back and hips still on the bench.

guideBrief.barPath: Slight arc from the lower chest up to over the shoulders
emphasise: Bar touches lower on the chest than a flat bench
